title: Where do these AI trading platforms actually fall short?
author: Low-Paper-5010
selftext:
Hi! I'm quite new to the AI trading space, but I've seen a lot of finance apps ship their own version of agentic trading this year and it has made me quite interested in learning more about how it works!

  
The tricky part is that all of the marketing I've sounds pretty identical, so I can't really tell which parts actually valuable features and useful once you're using it.



So, I was just curious, for anyone actually running one of these, what does yours do really well? And what does it still get wrong that you've kind of just learned to live with? Any thoughts would really help!

comments.author: Grundlefish
comments.body: People seem to backtest on stuff like crypto on the years that pumped astronomically. Most backtests, if you’d just bought and held the asset the whole time, you’d have made more money. Most algos don’t even beat the S&P 500, let alone the crypto golden years. Also, when backtesting, they often don’t account for the fact that the asset is spot and can’t be shorted as well - or at least couldn’t be in the years they are backtesting (crypto). Most algos you see are just hype to sell something, or the person plugging it just doesn’t understand that the results aren’t actually that impressive.
